description: The PICTURE character-string length bound (ISO §2023:13.18.40.3 SR4: 63 characters in the 2023 text) is 50 at COBOL-2002 - a RELAXATION, so a 51-to-63-character character-string-1 compiles at 2014 and 2023 and is rejected at COBOL-85 and COBOL-2002 with COBOL2146 (also under --permissive: a length error, not a removed construct). THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): §1985:VI.5.9.3 SR4 'The maximum number of characters allowed in the character-string is 30.'; §2002:13.16.38.2 SR4 'The maximum number of characters allowed in character-string-1 is 50.', §2002:F.2 item 94 recording the increase 'from 30 to 50'; §2014:13.18.40.2 SR4 'The maximum number of characters allowed in character-string-1 is 63.', and §2014:E.3 item 19 records the change: 'The maximum number of characters that may be specified in a picture character-string is increased from 50 to 63.' (VCR row 7.46). ONE bound, PictureAnalyzer.MaxStringLength(edition) (kb/Work PB4304).
display: a PICTURE character-string longer than 50 characters
rule1985: §1985:VI.5.9.3 SR4 (at most 30 characters in the PICTURE character-string)
vcr: VCR row 7.46 (PICTURE character-string bound 50 -> 63 at 2014); kb/Work PB4304
